draft.title: Stem-and-leaf plots
card: A stem-and-leaf plot splits each value into a stem and a leaf. For two-digit numbers, the stem is the tens digit and the leaf is the ones digit.
Example: 23 has stem 2 and leaf 3. The row 2 | 3 7 shows the values 23 and 27.
Stems go in order down the side. Leaves go in order along each row, smallest first. Write a note such as 2 | 3 means 23, so readers know what the digits stand for.
Every value in the data is kept, so you can read each one. Repeated values get a leaf each. Longer rows show where most values sit.
draft.remember: The stem holds the front digits, the leaf holds the last digit, and every value stays in the plot.

a.q: In a plot where 4 | 1 means 41, which values does the row 4 | 1 5 8 show?
a.why: The stem 4 is the tens digit, and each leaf is a ones digit. So the row shows 41, 45 and 48. The option 41, 15 and 18 treats the later leaves as tens digits.
a.clue: The stem is the tens digit for every leaf in the row.

b.q: Ben's test scores are 52, 47, 55, 61, 47 and 58. Which row of the plot shows the scores in the 40s?
b.why: Ben scored 47 twice, so the row needs two leaves of 7. The row 4 | 7 drops one score, because every value must be kept.
b.clue: Count how many scores are in the 40s, then give each one a leaf.
